The deliverable is identified as DEL-14-04, Analysis-run comparison engine.

DEL-14-04 supports objective OBJ-016.
Anticipated artifacts for DEL-14-04 are the run comparison engine and result delta tests.
The primary function is to implement unit-normalized result deltas for mapped entities, diagnostics, and settings.
The comparison subject is analysis runs and/or model states bounded by SOW-073; this deliverable focuses on analysis-run comparison.
The required comparison basis is stable IDs, manual mappings where required, unit-normalized result deltas, and tolerance profiles.
The analysis-run basis comprises exact model states, solver versions, settings, units, load cases, diagnostics, results, rule-pack references, library references, and result hashes.
Entity/result coverage includes mapped nodes, elements, supports, terminals, stress/result locations, diagnostics, and settings.
The role boundary is diagnostic/audit functionality only, excluding automatic external validation, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, and code-compliance determination.
The architecture basis is Rust core/application services with schema-first command/query/job result envelopes, JSON Schema 2020-12, and a JCS-compatible hash basis for hashed JSON payloads.
Applicable gates include Cargo, Vitest, Playwright, validation, and protected-content gates.

Open implementation decisions remain TBD: dependency versions, solver numerical library, public API transport, import/export format list, CI provider/coverage thresholds, physical package/container, comparison tolerance defaults, and mapping workflows.

DEL-14-04 exists to make analysis-run comparisons deterministic, unit-aware, traceable, and suitable for diagnostic/audit review; its output supports design iteration and review and does not decide external validation or professional reliance.
Keep comparison evidence tied to exact run/model-state basis, solver version, settings, units, load cases, diagnostics, result hashes, and relevant rule/library references.
Prefer stable IDs; use explicit manual mappings when stable IDs do not establish a safe comparison relationship.
Treat unit-bearing values as comparable only when unit and dimension metadata support the comparison; missing or ambiguous unit metadata is a diagnostic.
Preserve raw delta evidence separately from tolerance-based classification so tolerance profiles can change without rewriting source evidence; the exact output structure is TBD.
Keep diagnostics and settings in scope because the decomposition names them explicitly for DEL-14-04.
Preserve the professional boundary: comparison output is review evidence, not approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code compliance.
DEL-14-05 owns mapping/tolerance/export contracts; DEL-14-04 should consume those contracts rather than inventing mapping semantics.
OI-014 records comparison tolerance defaults and mapping workflows as TBD; do not hard-code defaults without human/product approval.
Unit normalization depends on accepted unit metadata and conversion governance; unsupported conversion semantics should remain TBD or become diagnostics.
Result export envelopes are the intended review/regression/report-consumption surface; avoid ad hoc result shapes once the schema contract is available.
JSON payload hashes use the accepted JCS-compatible basis where JSON payloads are hashed; non-JSON and binary partitioning remains TBD.
Fixtures, examples, and report sections must not embed protected standards text, protected tables, proprietary values, private project data, or private rule-pack payloads.
Trade-off: keep unresolved mapping, tolerance, and result-schema choices as TBD until upstream contracts are accepted, favoring contract maturity over early implementation.
Trade-off: preserve raw delta evidence and expose tolerance-classified outcomes as derived interpretation.
Trade-off: include enough diagnostics for review and audit while avoiding compliance/approval language.
Trade-off: cover mapped result entities, diagnostics, and settings while deferring export semantics and mapping/tolerance contract definition to DEL-14-05.
Concrete examples are TBD; future examples should use invented or permitted data, documented provenance, explicit units, and no protected standards text/tables or proprietary values.

Step 1: Establish the comparison input pair from exact analysis-run records, including model-state basis, solver version, settings, units, load cases, diagnostics, results, rule-pack references, library references, and result hashes; schema/API field names are TBD.

Step 2: Resolve comparison mapping, preferring stable-ID alignment where safe and using manual mappings where required by SOW-073, without inventing mapping workflow semantics; consume the DEL-14-05 contract when available.

Step 3: Validate unit comparability before computing deltas, comparing only same-dimension unit-bearing values after accepted normalization and emitting diagnostics for missing, ambiguous, or unsupported unit metadata.

Step 4: Compute result deltas for mapped comparison subjects (nodes, elements, supports, terminals, stress/result locations, diagnostics, settings) and preserve raw delta evidence before tolerance-based classification.
Step 5: Apply tolerance profiles using accepted tolerance profile contracts; defaults and mapping workflows remain TBD under OI-014.

Step 6: Produce deterministic comparison output using stable ordering and schema-first envelopes, preserving diagnostics, provenance, units, hashes/status boundaries, and professional-boundary notices.

Step 7: Create result delta tests covering deterministic repeatability, stable-ID matching, manual mapping, unit-normalized deltas, missing-unit diagnostics, settings deltas, diagnostic deltas, and tolerance classification, using only invented/public/permissive fixtures.

Scope: DEL-14-04 covers the backend feature slice for an analysis-run comparison engine, comparing two analysis runs and where applicable their bound model states using stable IDs, manual mappings, unit-normalized result deltas, diagnostics, settings, and tolerance profiles.

Scope exclusions: comprehensive commercial-prover result ingestion, external validation, professional approval, certification, sealing, authentication, automatic code-compliance determination, and protected standards-data content.
R-14-04-001: The engine shall compare analysis runs deterministically using stable IDs and manual mappings where required.

R-14-04-002: The engine shall treat analysis-run records as bound to exact model states, solver versions, settings, units, load cases, diagnostics, results, rule-pack references, library references, and result hashes.
R-14-04-003: The engine shall compute unit-normalized result deltas only where unit and dimension metadata allow valid comparison.

R-14-04-004: The engine shall include mapped nodes, elements, supports, terminals, stress/result locations, diagnostics, and settings within comparison scope where upstream result records expose them.
R-14-04-005: The engine shall use tolerance profiles for comparison classification.
R-14-04-006: The engine shall preserve professional-boundary language so comparison output is diagnostic/audit evidence and does not claim external validation or engineering acceptance.
R-14-04-007: The engine shall remain compatible with schema-first result/export envelopes rather than creating an ad hoc comparison result surface.
R-14-04-008: The engine shall not introduce protected standards text, protected tables, proprietary values, private rule-pack payloads, or invented engineering defaults into public artifacts.
R-14-04-009: The deliverable shall include result delta tests as an anticipated artifact.
